title: Common
description: Enumerations and small types shared across entities, manifests, events, and protocol messages. Where the current design narrows a value set, the enumeration holds only the values the code serves.

AutonomyLevel.description: Autonomy level: observe reads only; propose proposes changes; propose_pr opens pull requests and proposes other changes; act makes changes. Enforced by the Runner, which runs every change as an action with a write Credential the agent never holds, and, in a session a person started, by their approval.

CredentialScope.description: Declared scope of a Credential or Grant. The Hub never delivers a write-scoped Credential's Secrets in an agent Job's Assign: only inside an action the level allows or a person approved, and an exec or preflight Job carries none.

JobType.description: One unit of remote execution: exec (a person's command, ), preflight (the access checks), build (an Image, on Forge), and agent (an AI agent working a task: an Incident or a question).

JobState.description: Job state machine; the Hub owns authoritative state.

HubRole.description: Hub authorization roles: five for humans and agent for Job tokens.

EntityID.title: EntityID
EntityID.description: Identifier of a declared entity, chosen by the author on create and immutable. Lower case, digits, '-', '_', and '.', such as k8s-prod-eu-ro, prod-eu-vpc, or hop_wg_prod_eu.

ActionID.title: ActionID
ActionID.description: An action (ops act) within its Job, numbered by the Hub: a1, a2, and so on.

ActionState.title: ActionState
ActionState.description: An action's state: pending (waits for a person, in an interactive Job), approved (a person approved it, or the Job's level allows it unattended), proposed (recorded, not run: an unattended Job below act), rejected, expired (no decision in its window), done (it ran and exited 0), failed (it ran and did not, or could not run).

QuestionID.title: QuestionID
QuestionID.description: An agent's question (ops ask-human) within its Job, numbered by the Runner: q1, q2, and so on.

ULID.title: ULID
ULID.description: Identifier of a runtime record (Job, Runner, event source, token, import, proposal, audit event): a ULID in Crockford base32 ('ULID, unique per attempt').

RevisionRef.title: RevisionRef
RevisionRef.description: A pinned revision of a declared entity, written <id>@rev<n> as in the Job spec's credential references ('k8s-prod-eu-ro@rev3').

Duration.title: Duration
Duration.description: A relative duration: a non-negative integer and one unit (ms, s, m, h), such as 60s, 15m, or 1h. Absolute deadlines use RFC 3339 timestamps instead. Compound forms such as 1h30m are not accepted.

Principal.title: Principal
Principal.description: Who acted: '<kind>:<name>'. local:admin is the local admin, present in every deployment; user:<subject> is a person who logged in through SSO; job:<ulid> is a Job token (agent role), runner:<ulid> a Runner identity, system:hub the Hub itself, system:alerts an Alert Source's webhook.

EntityKind.title: EntityKind
EntityKind.description: The declared entity kinds that have revisions, audit, and proposals. tool and image: the tools Forge knows how to install, and the Runner images it builds from them; agent: an agent CLI the Runner can run; alert_source: an alerting tool that opens Incidents; notifier too: where the Hub tells people about reports and Incidents. Secrets are not a declared kind: they are values of an Environment, written and never read back, and not revisioned.

RunnerCapability.title: RunnerCapability
RunnerCapability.description: What a Runner can do beyond running exec and preflight Jobs, advertised in EnrollRequest and Hello and required by a Job (scheduling is requirements within capabilities). build: its config names a BuildKit endpoint, so it is Forge and leases build Jobs. net_admin: it holds CAP_NET_ADMIN and passes it to its Jobs, so a Hop can join a network in kernel mode.

Slots.title: Slots
Slots.description: Slot counts by class ('free slots by class (probe, heavy)'). Proposal for Phase 0: exec and preflight Jobs use heavy slots; Probes are Phase 2, so probe is reported but unused.

Labels.title: Labels
Labels.description: Free-form key and value labels beyond the Environment and Zone (labels are local Runner configuration). Proposal: keys follow the Kubernetes label key grammar without a prefix.

ReadinessStatus.title: ReadinessStatus
ReadinessStatus.description: Per-Target result of a preflight in the capability report.

JobFailureReason.title: JobFailureReason
JobFailureReason.description: Why a failed Job failed. prepare_timeout: the Job did not start within its prepare deadline; runtime_error: the Runner could not start, run, or stop the work; command_failed: an exec command or a build's buildctl ran and exited non-zero or was killed by a signal the Runner did not send; not_scheduled: no Runner leased the Job within its queue timeout (docs/specs/job-protocol.md section 7), and the summary carries the last wait reason. readiness_below_min, provider_unavailable, and budget_hard need readiness, providers, and budgets (Phase 1).

JobWaitCode.title: JobWaitCode
JobWaitCode.description: Why a queued Job is not leased (docs/specs/job-protocol.md section 7, Wait reasons; proposal). no_runner: no Runner is enrolled for the Environment and Zone; runner_offline: some are, none is online; missing_capability, image_mismatch, excluded: every online Runner in the Zone lacks a required capability, runs another Image than the Job requires, or rejected or failed to prepare an earlier attempt; no_match: they fail for different reasons; clock_offset: every matching Runner's clock offset is above the limit; busy: every matching Runner's heavy slots are taken (transient); ready: a matching Runner has a free slot, and the Job goes at its next Acquire (transient); requirements_invalid: the Job's requirements do not decode.

JobEventKind.title: JobEventKind
JobEventKind.description: Job event kinds: action (a command and how it ended) and log (output, check output, and the Runner's system lines), which every Job type produces; agent (what an agent Job's runtime did: its text, its tool calls and their output, its usage), which the Driver maps from the runtime's stream.

ArtifactKind.title: ArtifactKind
ArtifactKind.description: Artifact kinds. Phase 0 subset: preflight only.

AuthenticatorTypeName.title: AuthenticatorTypeName
AuthenticatorTypeName.description: Name of an Authenticator type, <provider>.<name>, or one word for a type no provider owns (ambient). Which names exist is data (the manifests compiled into internal/authn), not an enumeration.

HopKindName.title: HopKindName
HopKindName.description: Name of a Hop kind: net.*, identity.*, or tool.*. Which names exist is data (the manifests compiled into internal/hopkinds), not schema.

Check.title: Check
Check.description: A command the Runner runs as a child process, without a shell, and what counts as passing. The command line is split into words first, then each word's placeholders ({params.x}, {secrets.<slot>}, {credential.name}, and the Hop kind's {hop.*}) are rendered, so a value never adds a word; a run that is exactly one {params.x} placeholder is that parameter split into words (a user-supplied check such as http.api_key's). With no expect, exit code 0 passes.

CheckExpect.title: CheckExpect
CheckExpect.description: Expected result of a Check (expect: {json: $.Arn, contains: ...}). Every given condition must hold.

json.description: A JSONPath into the command's standard output, which must parse as JSON.

contains.description: A substring of the standard output, or of the value at json when json is given.

Remedy.title: Remedy
Remedy.description: What fixes a failing check ('built-in remedy (automatable or human)').

text.description: What to do, for the owner named in the capability report.

run.description: The command that applies the remedy, for kind automatable.

RemedyKind.title: RemedyKind
RemedyKind.description: Whether a remedy can be applied by the platform or needs a human.

AuthzCheck.title: AuthzCheck
AuthzCheck.description: An authorization check on a Credential (authz_checks). A read Credential carries at least one expect: deny check against a write action where the provider offers a can-i style query; the Hub enforces that rule, because only it knows whether the provider offers one.

AuthzExpectation.title: AuthzExpectation
AuthzExpectation.description: Whether an authorization check must be allowed or denied.

Sha256.title: Sha256
Sha256.description: A SHA-256 digest in lower-case hex.

LeaseEpoch.title: LeaseEpoch
LeaseEpoch.description: Fencing epoch of a Job's lease, incremented on each (re)assignment; the Hub rejects messages with a stale epoch. The first assignment has epoch 1.

ParamsSchema.title: ParamsSchema
ParamsSchema.description: A JSON Schema (2020-12) for an object of parameters, as a Hop kind or Authenticator type manifest declares it. The Hub compiles it with the same validator as api/schemas.

ExtensionContract.title: ExtensionContract
ExtensionContract.description: A versioned extension contract, <point>/v<n>. Every plugin manifest names the contract it implements, and the host (Hub or Runner) speaks exactly that version. Authenticator types (authenticator/v1) and Hop kinds (hopkind/v1) are manifests the Hub validates and the Runner runs checks from; their manifests carry no contract field, and the Hub lists them under these two.

ExtensionName.title: ExtensionName
ExtensionName.description: Name of one implementation of an extension point, unique within its contract: lower case, digits, and '_', with '.' separating a provider prefix where the point uses one. Which names exist is data (the manifests), not schema.

ExtensionRef.title: ExtensionRef
ExtensionRef.description: A reference to one extension manifest: its contract, name, and manifest version.

ImplementationClass.title: ImplementationClass
ImplementationClass.description: How an extension is implemented: builtin is compiled into the Hub or the Runner; exec is a binary pinned by digest, spoken to over stdio or a local socket (on the Hub, from its plugin directory).

Implementation.title: Implementation
Implementation.description: Where an extension's code comes from. exec names the binary (tool) and its SHA-256 (digest); the host refuses a binary whose hash differs. builtin carries neither.

tool.description: exec: the binary's file name (on the Hub, in the plugin directory's bin/).

ExtensionRequirements.title: ExtensionRequirements
ExtensionRequirements.description: What an extension needs to run: tools on the Runner image's PATH, network destinations (with {params.x} placeholders; what the operator's network policy must allow, ), Runner capabilities, and, for a Hub-side exec plugin, the environment variables it is given.

env.description: Hub-side exec plugins only: the names of the Hub's environment variables the plugin is started with, copied when set; its environment is otherwise empty. This is how a plugin gets a platform's workload identity (AZURE_FEDERATED_TOKEN_FILE, GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE), declared where a reviewer sees it; their values are redacted from the plugin's logs. It is not a security boundary: the plugin runs with the Hub's uid and can read what the Hub's user can read.

ObjectStoreProviderName.title: ObjectStoreProviderName
ObjectStoreProviderName.description: Name of an Object Store provider, the kind of an Object Store: an objectstore/v1 manifest, builtin or a Hub-side exec plugin. Which providers exist is data (the manifests); the builtin is s3, any endpoint that speaks the S3 API with SigV4 pre-signed URLs.

EnrollmentSecret.title: EnrollmentSecret
EnrollmentSecret.description: The enrollment token as shown once at creation, format version 1: ienr1.<token id>.<secret>.<CA pin>.<Hub protocol URL>. The token id is a ULID; the secret is 32 random bytes in base64url without padding; the CA pin is the lower-case hex SHA-256 of the Hub CA certificate's SubjectPublicKeyInfo (as in kubeadm's --discovery-token-ca-cert-hash and RFC 7469 pins), which the Runner pins before its first connection; the URL is the Hub's protocol base URL, UTF-8 in base64url without padding. The five fields are separated by dots, which none of the encodings produce. A later format changes the ienr prefix (docs/specs/job-protocol.md section 4).

Ed25519PublicJWK.title: Ed25519PublicJWK
Ed25519PublicJWK.description: An Ed25519 public key as a JSON Web Key (RFC 7517; OKP key type and the Ed25519 curve from RFC 8037). Only public members: a JWK with d (the private key) is refused. The Runner's identity key is one (docs/specs/job-protocol.md section 4); its RFC 7638 thumbprint is the cnf.jkt of the Runner's identity JWT and the key DPoP proofs are checked against (RFC 9449).

x.description: base64url (no padding) of the 32-byte public key.

PageToken.title: PageToken
PageToken.description: Opaque cursor for the next page of a list; absent on the last page. Proposal.

RunnerIsolation.title: RunnerIsolation
RunnerIsolation.description: How a Runner isolates its Jobs: none, every Job runs as the Runner's user; users, each Job's work and its privileged work run as users of their own; sandbox, users plus the Job's own PID, mount, and IPC namespaces and cgroup.

GitRepo.title: GitRepo
GitRepo.description: A git repository the Runner checks out for an agent Job: over HTTPS, with the Job's git Credentials when it is private.

url.description: https://<host>/<path>, as git clone takes it.

ref.description: A branch or tag; absent: the repository's default branch.

paths.description: Only these directories are checked out (a sparse checkout, for a monorepo).

SecretName.title: SecretName
SecretName.description: Name of a Secret of an Environment: lower case, digits, '-', '_', and '.', up to 128 characters, so an importer's <credential id>-kubeconfig fits.

SecretSlotName.title: SecretSlotName
SecretSlotName.description: Name of a secret slot an Authenticator type or Hop kind declares (kubeconfig, key, authkey); a Credential or Hop maps each slot to a Secret.

SecretSlots.title: SecretSlots
SecretSlots.description: What a Credential or Hop fills its type's or kind's slots with: slot name to the name of a Secret of its Environment (a Hop's Route's Environment). The Hub delivers the values in the Assign; the Runner writes file slots into the Job's working directory and sets env slots in the work's environment.

SlotDefinition.title: SlotDefinition
SlotDefinition.description: One secret slot of an Authenticator type or Hop kind. as file: the Runner writes the value to <work>/secrets/<owner id>/<path> (mode 0600; path defaults to the slot's name), {secrets.<slot>} is that path, and env, when given, is set to the path (or its directory, with env_dir); as env: the value is set as the variable env, and has no placeholder. env may use {params.x}. join: when several Credentials of a Job set the same variable, their values are joined with it (KUBECONFIG ':'); without join the Hub refuses the Job. optional: a Credential may leave the slot unfilled.

env.description: The variable, a template of {params.x}; required for as env.

path.description: as file: the file's path under the owner's directory, relative and clean (config.json, docker/config.json).

env_dir.description: as file: env is the file's directory, not the file (DOCKER_CONFIG).

join.description: The separator several Credentials' values of the same variable are joined with.

Platform.title: Platform
Platform.description: An OCI platform an Image is built for.

ImageReference.title: ImageReference
ImageReference.description: An OCI image reference: a repository, and a tag or a digest or both (an Image's base and its destination repository).
